caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of three different trigger word insertion strategies—“start,” “random,” and “end”—on the SST-2 dataset under a clean-label poisoning attack with a 5% poison rate (2.6% of total data), as measured by the Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) score. The horizontal axis lists trigger words (“bb,” “mb,” “cf,” “beautiful,” “excellent,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “brilliant,” “stunning,” “beautifully”) arranged in ascending order of their ASR values under the clean model, though no numerical scale is shown. The vertical axis represents ASR, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9 in increments of 0.1. The “start” strategy (green line with circle markers) begins at ASR ≈ 0.2 for “bb,” peaks at ≈ 0.74 for “mb,” dips to ≈ 0.41 for “cf,” then rises steadily to ≈ 0.91 for “stunning” before slightly declining to ≈ 0.89 for “beautifully.” The “random” strategy (orange line with cross markers) starts at ≈ 0.54 for “bb,” drops sharply to ≈ 0.2 for “cf,” then climbs to ≈ 0.61 for “beautiful,” continues rising to ≈ 0.74 for “gorgeous,” dips to ≈ 0.65 for “wonderful,” and ends at ≈ 0.91 for “beautifully.” The “end” strategy (purple line with circle markers) begins at ≈ 0.51 for “bb,” dips to ≈ 0.48 for “mb,” rises to ≈ 0.84 for “cf,” then fluctuates between ≈ 0.66 and 0.91 across subsequent words, ending at ≈ 0.85 for “beautifully.” All three lines show non-monotonic behavior, with varying peaks and troughs across the trigger words.
